extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate/graduate students and researchers in enumerative combinatorics and poset/lattice theory (readers solving textbook exercises)
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of exercise prompts about posets, lattices, order polynomials, zeta/characteristic polynomials, Eulerian/binomial/differential/triangular posets, cd-indexes, and related enumerative and algebraic properties; each item asks to prove, compute, characterize, or construct examples. Intended as textbook problem solving in enumerative combinatorics and poset theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: 155(a) — αP(S) depends only on multiset of rank-differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P be a finite graded poset of rank n with ˆ0 and ˆ1, and suppose every interval is self-dual. For S = {n1, n2, ..., ns} ⊂ [n−1], show that αP(S) depends only on the multiset of numbers n1, n2−n1, n3−n2, ..., ns−n{s−1} (not on their order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove invariance of αP(S) under permutation of those successive differences; uses the interval self-duality hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: 155(b) — distributive lattice with self-dual intervals is product of chains
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L be a finite distributive lattice for which every interval is self-dual. Show that L is a product of chains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This asks to deduce a structural classification (product of chains). A stronger result is referenced (Exercise 3.166).

rubrics_metrics.name: 155(c) — classify finite modular lattices with self-dual intervals
rubrics_metrics.description: Find all finite modular lattices for which every interval is self-dual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 5-point exercise: determine all modular lattices satisfying the interval self-duality property.

rubrics_metrics.name: 156 — compute β for P = N×N on finite S
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P = N×N (infinite). For finite S ⊂ P of form S = {m1, m2, ..., ms} ⊂ N, define αP(S) and βP(S) as in Section 3.13 and show β_{N×N}(S) = m1(m2−m1−1)(m3−m2−1)···(ms−m{s−1}−1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute β for infinite grid poset restricted to finite S; product formula given in statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: 157(a) — expression for ∆_{k+1} Z(P,0) equals αP(S)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P be finite graded rank n with ˆ0 and ˆ1. Show that ∆_{k+1} Z(P,0) = sum_{S⊆[n−1], #S=k} αP(S).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relates finite differences of zeta polynomial at 0 to α-values summed over S of fixed size.

rubrics_metrics.name: 157(b) — series for Z(P,m) in terms of βk
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that (1−x)^{n+1} ∑_{m≥0} Z(P,m) x^m = ∑_{k≥0} β_k x^{k+1}, where β_k = ∑_{S⊆[n−1], #S=k} β_P(S).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives generating-function relation between zeta polynomial and β-coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: 157(c) — characteristic polynomial via βP([k])
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that the characteristic polynomial χ_P(q) = ∑_{k≥0} (−1)^k w_k q^{n−k} where (−1)^k w_k = β_P([k−1]) + β_P([k]). (Set βP([n]) = βP([−1]) = 0.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expresses coefficients of characteristic polynomial in terms of β-values for initial intervals [k].

rubrics_metrics.name: 158(a) — zeta polynomial of P_{k,t}
rubrics_metrics.description: Define P_{k,t} the poset of partitions π of [kt] with each block size divisible by k and condition (ii) about interleaving blocks. Show combinatorially Z(P_{k,t}, n+1) = ((kn+1)^t t^t) / t! (minus 1?) (statement gives formula: ((kn+1)^t t^t) / t! − 1?).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove given closed form for zeta polynomial of this partition subposet using combinatorial counting.

rubrics_metrics.name: 158(b) — size and Möbius of P_{1,t}
rubrics_metrics.description: Note P_{k,t} has ˆ1 and P_{1,t} has ˆ0. Use (a) to show P_{1,t} has C_t elements (Catalan number) and µ_{P_{1,t}}(ˆ0,ˆ1)= (−1)^{t−1} C_{t−1} (?) as indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate to Catalan numbers; use earlier zeta polynomial.

rubrics_metrics.name: 158(c) — P_{2,t} is Int(P_{1,t})
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that P_{2,t} is isomorphic to Int(P_{1,t}), the poset of intervals of P_{1,t}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish poset isomorphism between partitions with block sizes divisible by 2 and interval poset.

rubrics_metrics.name: 158(d) — α_{P_{k,t}}(S) formula for certain S
rubrics_metrics.description: If P_{k,t} is graded of rank t−1 and S = {m1,...,ms} ⊆ [0,t−2], show α_{P_{k,t}}(S) equals an explicit product formula involving binomial-like factors: (1/t) * product_{i} binomial(kt, mi − mi−1) etc (statement provides detailed product).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute α for rank-selected subsets S in this poset; formula in exercise.

rubrics_metrics.name: 158(e) — number of maximal chains of P_{k,t}
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce that P_{k,t} has (k(kt)! t)/... (exercise states P_{k,t} has (1/t) * ... maximal chains).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use part (d) to count maximal chains explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: 158(f) — counting partitions of given type in P_{1,t}
rubrics_metrics.description: Let λ ⊢ t with part sizes λ1,λ2,... Show the number N_λ of π ∈ P_{1,t} of type λ (i.e., with blocks of sizes λ1,λ2,...) is N_λ = (t! / ∏ i m_i(λ)! ∏ j (j!)^{m_j(λ)}) where m_j(λ) denotes multiplicity of part size j.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard multinomial/counting-of-set-partitions formula specialized to P_{1,t}.

rubrics_metrics.name: 158(g) — P_{1,t} supersolvable
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Exercise 3.125 to show that P_{1,t} is a supersolvable lattice (though not semimodular for t ≥ 4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish supersolvability property and note semimodularity fails when t is large.

rubrics_metrics.name: 159 — interval [ˆ0,w] in absolute order equals P_{1,n}
rubrics_metrics.description: Define absolute order A(S_n) on S_n by u ⋖ v if v=(i,j)u and v has one fewer cycle. Show that if w is an n-cycle then [ˆ0,w] ≅ P_{1,n} (from Ex.3.158).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate the absolute order intervals on permutations to the partition poset P_{1,n}.

rubrics_metrics.name: 160 — equivalence classes of labelings equals acyclic orientations
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix p-element poset P. Define equivalence of labelings ω,ω' : P→[p] by (P,ω) ≅ (P,ω'). Show number of equivalence classes equals number of acyclic orientations of the Hasse diagram of P (undirected).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate labeling equivalence to orientations; reference Ex.3.109 for acyclic orientations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 161 — shuffles and descent-set dependence
rubrics_metrics.description: Given permutations u and v on disjoint sets of sizes j,k, define Sh(u,v). Show #Sh(u,v)=binomial(j+k,j) and that the number of permutations in Sh(u,v) with descent set S depends only on D(u) and D(v) (descent sets of u and v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use theory of (P,ω)-partitions for descent-set invariance in shuffles.

rubrics_metrics.name: 162(a) — WP for disjoint union P1+P2 factorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P1,P2 disjoint posets with sizes p1,p2 and labeling ω of P1+P2. Let ωi be labeling on Pi preserving relative order. Show WP_{P1+P2,ω}(x) = binomial(p1+p2,p1)_x WP_{P1,ω1}(x) WP_{P2,ω2}(x), where q-binomial coefficient in variable x is indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove generating-function/product formula for WP under disjoint union using q-binomial.

rubrics_metrics.name: 162(b) — shuffle generalization product formula
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Π_n be partition of [n] into blocks Bi with sizes bi and permutations wi of Bi. Define shuffles of w1,...,wk. Show identity: ∑_{w∈sh(w1,...,wk)} x^{maj(w)} = (n choose b1,...,bk)_x ∏_{i} x^{maj(wi)}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives q-multinomial factorization for maj generating function over shuffles; (3.126) referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: 162(c) — minimal maj(w) for shuffles and uniqueness
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce from (b) that minimum maj(w) over shuffles equals sum maj(wi) and is achieved uniquely; describe extremal permutation w explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterize and construct unique permutation achieving minimal major index among shuffles.

rubrics_metrics.name: 163(a) — monotonicity of Ω_P(m)m^{-p}
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P be p-element poset with order polynomial Ω_P(m). Show Ω_P(m)m^{-p} is eventually decreasing and strictly decreasing if P not antichain (as m→∞).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze asymptotic monotonicity properties of scaled order polynomial.

rubrics_metrics.name: 163(b) — is Ω_P(m)m^{-p} decreasing for all m?
rubrics_metrics.description: Question: Is Ω_P(m)m^{-p} decreasing for all m≥1 (not just eventually)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problem asks to determine monotonicity for all m or give counterexamples.

rubrics_metrics.name: 164 — nonnegativity of coefficients of Ω_P(m)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P finite poset. Does the order polynomial Ω_P(m) always have nonnegative coefficients?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate coefficient sign-positivity of order polynomial in m.

rubrics_metrics.name: 165 — real-rootedness of (P,ω)-Eulerian polynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: Let (P,ω) be finite labeled poset. Does AP,ω(x) have only real zeros? What if ω is a natural labeling?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Question about real-rootedness/spectral properties of Eulerian polynomials for labeled posets.

rubrics_metrics.name: 166(a) — symmetry of GP(x) if and only if P disjoint union of chains
rubrics_metrics.description: For natural labeling ω, define GP(x) symmetric function. Show GP(x) symmetric iff P is disjoint union of chains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use characterization in terms of α_{J(P)}(S) depending only on multisets (see note linking to Ex.3.155).

rubrics_metrics.name: 166(b) — characterization of GP,ω symmetric via convex subsets of N×N
rubrics_metrics.description: Show GP,ω(x) symmetric iff P is isomorphic to a finite convex subset of N×N labeled with inequalities ω(i,j)>ω(i+1,j) and ω(i,j)<ω(i,j+1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives structural geometric characterization for symmetry of GP,ω.

rubrics_metrics.name: 167(a) — order polynomial for union of two chains with added ˆ0/ˆ1
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P be disjoint union of two chains with possible added ˆ0/ˆ1 and labeling with adjacent labels on Hasse edges. Show all linear extensions have same number of descents and give explicit formula for Ω_{P,ω}(m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute order polynomial explicitly for these small structured posets; two examples in Figure 3.55.

rubrics_metrics.name: 167(b) — characterization when all linear extensions have same descents
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that if all linear extensions of (P,ω) have the same number of descents, then P is ordinal sum of posets of type (a) and describe possible labelings ω.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify posets/labelings giving constant descent number across linear extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 168 — product formula for WP(x) for certain naturally labelled poset
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P finite naturally labelled poset where every connected order ideal is either principal or uniquely decomposable as union of two connected ideals. Show WP(x) = n! ∏_{I} (1 / (#I1 + #I2 choose #I1) ) where product runs over connected order ideals I and I1,I2 are incomparable connected ideals whose union is I. Example in Figure 3.56 yields explicit WP(x)=1+x+2x^2+... etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive product formula for WP based on connected order ideals; compute example.

rubrics_metrics.name: 169(a) — rational form for AM(x) for multiset permutations
rubrics_metrics.description: Let M be multiset with multiplicities r1,...,rm and SM permutations. Define AM(x)=∑_{w∈SM} x^{1+des(w)} and show ∑_{n≥0} (coeffs given) AM(x) / (1−x)^{r+1} = ... (exercise gives generating function rational form).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain rational generating function for multiset Eulerian polynomial AM(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: 169(b) — coefficients of AM(x) for m=2
rubrics_metrics.description: Find coefficients of AM(x) explicitly in case m=2 (two-letter multiset).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carry out explicit combinatorial enumeration for small alphabet.

rubrics_metrics.name: 170 — classify pleasant posets and examples (a)-(i)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define pleasant poset P: rank-generating function of L=J(P) equals ∏_{t∈P} (1−q^{ρ(t)+2})/(1−q^{ρ(t)+1}). In (a)–(g) show listed posets are pleasant; (h) and (i) ask for expressions and classification; (i) Are there other nice classes and can all pleasant posets be classified?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple subproblems verifying pleasantness for various product/ordinal sum constructions and asking for broader classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: 171(a) — UP,ω,m(q) equals F(J(m×P),q)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define UP,ω,m(q)=∑_{(P,ω)-partitions σ:P→[0,m]} q^{|σ|}. Show UP,m(q)=F(J(m×P),q), the rank-generating function of J(m×P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relates order polynomial variant to rank-generating function of product poset's ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: 171(b) — decomposition of WP,ω(q) into WP,ω,i(q)
rubrics_metrics.description: For #P=p and 0≤i≤p−1 define WP,ω,i(q)=∑_{w} q^{maj(w)} where w in L(P,ω) has exactly i descents. Show WP,ω(q)=∑_{i} WP,ω,i(q) and UP,m(q) = ∑_{i=0}^{p} binomial(p+m−i,p) WP,ω,i(q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives combinatorial decomposition and binomial-weighted sum (equation (3.127),(3.128)).

rubrics_metrics.name: 171(c) — dual labeling reciprocity
rubrics_metrics.description: Let ω* labeling of dual P* by ω*(t)=p+1−ω(t). Show WP_{P*,ω*,i}(q) = q^{pi} WP_{P,ω,i}(1/q) and UP_{P*,ω*,m}(q) = q^{pm} UP_{P,ω,m}(1/q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: q-reciprocity relations between dual poset generating polynomials (equations (3.129),(3.130)).

rubrics_metrics.name: 171(d) — generalized binomial coefficient identity extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Use given identity to define generalized q-binomial coefficients for integer parameters and show specific transformation/formula holds for negative or general a,b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytic extension and transformation of q-binomial coefficients; used in (e).

rubrics_metrics.name: 171(e) — UP,ω,m(q) for any integer m via reciprocity
rubrics_metrics.description: Equation (3.96) and (d) allow definition of UP,ω,m(q) for any integer m; show expression for UP,ω,−m(q) as sum over (P,ω)-partitions τ:P→[0,m] of (−1)^p q^{−|τ|}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extend UP polynomials to negative m using reciprocity and signed sums.

rubrics_metrics.name: 171(f) — degree of WP,i(q) equals sum of largest i elements of M(P)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let M(P) and δ-r values as in Sect.3.15.4. Show degree of WP,i(q) equals sum of largest i elements of M(P). If P graded of rank ℓ then M(P) is [p−1] with ∆ values etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connect combinatorial maxdeg to multiset M(P) and rank/grading properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: 172(a) — Gaussian poset components are Gaussian
rubrics_metrics.description: Define Gaussian poset P by existence of integers h1,...,hp>0 such that UP,m(q)=∏_{i=1}^p (q^{m+hi}−1)/(q^{hi}−1) for all m. Show P Gaussian iff every connected component is Gaussian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decomposability criterion for Gaussian property.

rubrics_metrics.name: 172(b) — connected Gaussian poset is graded with equal chain lengths
rubrics_metrics.description: If P connected and Gaussian then every maximal chain of P has same length ℓ (so P graded of rank ℓ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deduces gradedness from Gaussian condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: 172(c) — multisets of 1+ρ(t) coincide
rubrics_metrics.description: If P connected Gaussian with rank ρ, show multisets {1+ρ(t) : t∈P} coincide with {h1,...,hp}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links h-values in Gaussian factorization with rank-based multiset.

rubrics_metrics.name: 172(d) — inequality for ordered h-values in connected Gaussian poset
rubrics_metrics.description: Label hi in nondecreasing order and show hi + h_{p+1−i} = ℓ(P) + 2 for 1≤i≤p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symmetry relation among h-values in connected Gaussian posets.

rubrics_metrics.name: 172(e) — minimal covers for rank-one elements in Gaussian poset
rubrics_metrics.description: If P connected Gaussian show every element of rank 1 covers exactly one minimal element of P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structural restriction deduced from Gaussian property.

rubrics_metrics.name: 172(f) — list of connected Gaussian posets
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that various poset families (products, J(2^r), ordinal sums etc listed) are Gaussian; part (g) asks if there are others or whether connected Gaussian poset must be distributive lattice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples and ask classification question.

rubrics_metrics.name: 173(a) — sign-grading iff P graded for natural labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Define sign-grading ϵ on labeled poset (P,ω). Show that if ω is natural then ϵ is a sign-grading iff P is graded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relates sign-grading notion to graded posets under natural labeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: 173(b) — existence of labeling giving sign-grading iff all maximal chain lengths same parity
rubrics_metrics.description: Show finite poset P has a labeling ω giving sign-grading iff lengths of all maximal chains have the same parity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterizes possibility of sign-graded labeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: 173(c) — relation of Eulerian polynomials under different sign-gradings
rubrics_metrics.description: If ω and ω' give sign-gradings ϵ and ϵ', show xr(ϵ)/2 A_{P,ω}(x) = xr(ϵ')/2 A_{P,ω'}(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relates Eulerian polynomials via centers of symmetry determined by rank of sign-grading.

rubrics_metrics.name: 173(d) — canonical labeling existence for sign-graded poset
rubrics_metrics.description: If (P,ω) is sign-graded with rank function ρ taking values 0 and 1 and ρ(s)<ρ(t) implies ω(s)<ω(t), call ω canonical. Show every sign-graded poset has a canonical labeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct canonical labeling; Figure 3.57 shows example.

rubrics_metrics.name: 173(e) — adding cover relation preserves sign-grading and canonical labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Let (P,ω) sign-graded and ω canonical. For s,t with ρ(t)=ρ(s)+1 form P' by adjoining s<t and P'' by adjoining s>t. Show P' and P'' are sign-graded and ω canonical for both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closure property under adding one cover relation; Figure 3.58 example.

rubrics_metrics.name: 173(f) — multiplicative decomposition of (P,ω)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show (P,ω) = (P',ω) ∪_L (P'',ω) and WP,ω(x) decomposes correspondingly (L-product).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relates decomposition to generating-function sum/product structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: 173(g) — AP,ω(x) as sum of symmetric terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Iterate decomposition procedure to express AP,ω(x) as sum of terms xb A'_a(x) ... where each term is symmetric with same center; b and a_i described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows decomposition into symmetric summands thus structural symmetry of AP,ω.

rubrics_metrics.name: 173(h) — coefficients of AP,ω(x) symmetric and unimodal
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce from (g) that coefficients of AP,ω(x) are symmetric and unimodal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequence of decomposition into symmetric terms with same center.

rubrics_metrics.name: 173(i) — carry out procedure for shown poset
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the iterative decomposition to the poset in Figure 3.59 (naturally labelled) and demonstrate resulting form of AP,ω.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete exercise to practice procedure and observe symmetry/unimodality.

rubrics_metrics.name: 174(a) — semi-Eulerian iff intervals except possibly whole poset balanced odd/even ranks
rubrics_metrics.description: Show finite graded poset with ˆ0 and ˆ1 is semi-Eulerian iff for all s<t (except possibly (ˆ0,ˆ1)) the interval [s,t] has as many elements of odd rank as even rank. P Eulerian if in addition whole P has equal numbers odd/even ranks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterize semi-Eulerian via parity counts in intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: 174(b) — relation between Z(P,m) and µP(ˆ0,ˆ1) for semi-Eulerian
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relates zeta polynomial parity property to Möbius function for semi-Eulerian poset rank n.

rubrics_metrics.name: 174(c) — semi-Eulerian poset of odd rank is Eulerian
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that a semi-Eulerian poset of odd rank n is Eulerian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parity argument yields full Eulerian property when rank odd.

rubrics_metrics.name: 175(a) — join construction preserves Eulerian
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose P and Q Eulerian; let P' = P ∪ {ˆ0} and Q' = Q ∪ {ˆ0} and R = (P' ∪ Q')  acksomething (text indicates construct R). Show R is Eulerian. (Ordinal-sum/union construction.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise about combining Eulerian posets to produce a new Eulerian poset (ordinal-sum like operation).

rubrics_metrics.name: 176(a) — compute β_{P_n}(S) for ordinal sum of n copies of 21
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Pn be ordinal sum of n copies of 21 with ˆ0 adjoined (illustration Fig.3.60). Compute β_{Pn}(S) for all S⊆[n].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerative computation specific to this constructed poset.

rubrics_metrics.name: 176(b) — compute Z(Pn,m) via (a) and Ex.3.157(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use (a) and Ex.3.157(b) to compute Z(Pn,m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply previous relationships between β and zeta polynomial.

rubrics_metrics.name: 176(c) — compute f(Pn,x) and g(Pn,x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute polynomials f(Pn,x) and g(Pn,x) (Section 3.16) for Pn, given Pn Eulerian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute face and g-polynomials for this Eulerian poset.

rubrics_metrics.name: 177(a) — Ln lattice of cube faces is Int(Bn) with ˆ0 adjoined
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Ln lattice of faces of n-cube. Show Ln ≅ Int(B_n) with ˆ0 adjoined, where B_n boolean algebra rank n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish isomorphism between cube face lattice and interval lattice of boolean algebra.

rubrics_metrics.name: 177(b) — Ln isomorphic to Λ_n with ˆ0 adjoined
rubrics_metrics.description: Show Ln ≅ Λ_n with ˆ0 adjoined, where Λ is three-element poset (diagram given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative structural description for cube face lattice.

rubrics_metrics.name: 177(c) — Ln isomorphic to chains of Pn excluding endpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Pn from Ex.3.176. Show Ln ≅ poset of chains of Pn that don't contain ˆ0 and ˆ1 (including empty chain), ordered by reverse inclusion, with ˆ0 adjoined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct isomorphism using chain-poset correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: 177(d) — compute β_{Ln}(S) via D_{n+1}(S,i+1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For S⊆[n] show β_{Ln}(S)=∑_{i=0}^n D_{n+1}(S,i+1) where D_m(T,j) counts permutations of [m] with descent set T and last element j.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express flag h-vector entries of Ln in terms of permutation descent-last-element statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: 177(e) — compute Z(Ln,m)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute zeta polynomial Z(Ln,m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumeration using known combinatorial structures of cube faces.

rubrics_metrics.name: 177(f) — compute g(Ln,x) and show formula
rubrics_metrics.description: Since Ln is face lattice of convex polytope and Eulerian, compute g(Ln,x) and show g(Ln,x)=1/(n+1)∑ a_i x^i where a_i counts plane trees with certain vertex-degree property; f(Ln,1)=2^n and g(Ln,1)=Catalan-related identity given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connect g-polynomial coefficients to plane tree enumeration; example and values provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: 177(g) — combinatorial interpretation of g(Ln,x) coefficients via plane trees
rubrics_metrics.description: Use (f) to show g(Ln,x)=∑_{i} a_i x^i where a_i counts plane trees with n+1 vertices and exactly i vertices of at least two children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish bijection/contact with plane tree statistics; Fig.3.61 example for n=3.

rubrics_metrics.name: 178 — exponential generating function for chains in Ln
rubrics_metrics.description: Let f(n) be total number of chains containing ˆ0 and ˆ1 in Ln. Show ∑_{n≥0} f(n) x^n / n! = 2 e^x / e^{2x} = 2 e^{-x}. (Statement shows 2 e^x / e^{2x} = 2 e^{-x} and equals series etc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive EGF identity for chain counts in cube face lattice.

rubrics_metrics.name: 179 — nonnegativity of g(L,x) coefficients for convex polytope face lattice
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L be face lattice of convex polytope. Show coefficients of g(L,x) are nonnegative (equivalently coefficients of f(L,x) are nonnegative and unimodal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove positivity/unimodality properties for g and f polynomials of polytopal Eulerian lattices.

rubrics_metrics.name: 180(a) — construct Eulerian lattice L_{n,d}
rubrics_metrics.description: For n,d≥1 with n≥d+1 define L'_{n,d} poset of subsets S⊆[n] satisfying special parity/containment condition into a d-subset; let L_{n,d}=L'_{n,d} with ˆ1 adjoined. Show L_{n,d} is Eulerian lattice of rank d+1. Figure 3.62 shows L_{4,2}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct and verify Eulerian property for these subset-lattices.

rubrics_metrics.name: 180(b) — number of rank-k elements in L_{n,d}
rubrics_metrics.description: Show L_{n,d} has binomial-number of elements of rank k for bounds given: ... expression in terms of n,k,d etc (exercise provides formula).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count elements of given rank in these lattices.

rubrics_metrics.name: 181(a) — truncation uniqueness of Eulerian lattice vs boolean algebra
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L be Eulerian lattice rank d+1 and suppose truncation L0∪...∪L_{⌈(d+1)/2⌉} is isomorphic to that of boolean algebra B_n of rank n. Does it follow n=d+1 and L≅M? Exercise asks to analyze uniqueness and boundaries; best possible examples referenced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate when partial truncations determine full lattice.

rubrics_metrics.name: 181(b) — question for Eulerian poset context
rubrics_metrics.description: What if we only assume L is Eulerian poset (not lattice)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generalize/relax conditions and consider consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: 182 — Γ_P Eulerian lattice from P-compatible partitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P finite poset and π partition into connected blocks; define partial order on blocks by existence of comparable elements; if relation is a partial order call π P-compatible. Let Γ_P be set of all P-compatible partitions ordered by refinement. Show Γ_P is Eulerian lattice (Fig.3.63 example).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove that P-compatible partition lattice is Eulerian and lattice-structured.

rubrics_metrics.name: 183(a) — Bruhat order gradedness and rank-generating function
rubrics_metrics.description: Define strong Bruhat order on S_n by cover relations v⋖w if w=(i,j)v and inv(w)=inv(v)+1. Show S_n under Bruhat order is graded with ρ(w)=inv(w) and rank-generating function F(S_n,q) = [n]!.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish basic graded poset structure of Bruhat order.

rubrics_metrics.name: 183(b) — characterization via triangular array T_w
rubrics_metrics.description: Given triangular array T_w of permutation w, show v≤w in Bruhat order iff T_v ≤ T_w component-wise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterize Bruhat order by component-wise comparison of insertion-like triangular arrays.

rubrics_metrics.name: 183(c) — S_n Eulerian
rubrics_metrics.description: Show S_n (Bruhat order) is Eulerian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove Eulerian property for Bruhat poset.

rubrics_metrics.name: 183(d) — count of cover relations in S_n
rubrics_metrics.description: Show number of cover relations in S_n is (n+1)!(H_{n+1}−1/(n+1)) where H_{n+1}=1+1/2+...+1/(n+1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerative formula for cover relations count in Bruhat order.

rubrics_metrics.name: 183(e) — Tv component-wise ordering characterization restated
rubrics_metrics.description: Same as (b): v≤w iff T_v≤T_w (component-wise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat/solidify equivalence characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: 183(f) — boolean-interval characterization count
rubrics_metrics.description: Find number of w in S_n for which interval [ˆ0,w] is boolean algebra; answer should avoid sums/products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterize permutations yielding boolean lower intervals and count them combinatorially.

rubrics_metrics.name: 183(g) — product of weights over maximal chains equals r!
rubrics_metrics.description: For cover v⋖w define weight ω(v,w)=..., for maximal chain C set ω(C)=∏ ω(vi−1,vi). Show ∑_{C} ω(C)=r! where C ranges over maximal chains in interval [ˆ0,ˆ1] of S_n and r is chain length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted chain-sum identity to be proven; compare to similar results later.

rubrics_metrics.name: 184 — In involution poset is Eulerian
rubrics_metrics.description: Let I_n be subposet of involutions in S_n under Bruhat order. Show I_n is Eulerian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove Eulerian property restricted to involutions subset.

rubrics_metrics.name: 185(a) — weak order W(S_n) gradedness
rubrics_metrics.description: Define weak Bruhat order covers w=v with adjacent transposition and inv increases by 1. Show W(S_n) graded with ρ(w)=inv(w) and rank-generating function F(W(S_n),q)=(n)!.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous gradedness check for weak order.

rubrics_metrics.name: 185(b) — weak order is a lattice
rubrics_metrics.description: Show W(S_n) is a lattice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove existence of join and meet for weak order.

rubrics_metrics.name: 185(c) — number of cover relations in W(S_n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show number of cover relations in W(S_n) is (n choose 2) n! / 2? (exercise indicates formula (n−1)!/2? full statement abbreviated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute enumerative formula for cover relations in weak order.

rubrics_metrics.name: 185(d) — Möbius function of W(S_n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show µ(v,w) = (−1)^k if w can be obtained from v by reversing elements in each of k+1 disjoint increasing factors of v; otherwise 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterize Möbius function on weak order by combinatorial factorization of permutations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 185(e) — zeta polynomial of W(S_n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show Z(W(S_n),j)=binomial(n−1,j−1) for 1≤j≤n (? exercise statement gives formula); verify generating values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive zeta polynomial values for weak order interval counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: 185(f) — pattern-avoidance characterization for boolean intervals
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterize permutations w in W(S_n) for which [ˆ0,w] is boolean algebra in terms of pattern avoidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide pattern-avoidance criteria equivalent to boolean-interval property.

rubrics_metrics.name: 185(g) — count of elements with boolean interval in W(S_n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Find number of w in W(S_n) for which [ˆ0,w] is boolean algebra; answer should avoid sums/products; more generally find generating function ∑_{such w} q^{rank(w)} x^{n}/n!.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerative/generating-function problem for boolean-interval permutations in weak order.

rubrics_metrics.name: 185(h) — generating function for intervals isomorphic to boolean B_i
rubrics_metrics.description: Let f(n,i) be total number intervals of W(S_n) isomorphic to B_i. Show ∑_{n,i} f(n,i) q^i x^n / n! equals a specific rational-exponential series (exercise provides expansion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute bivariate EGF for counts of boolean subintervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: 185(i) — distributive interval count in W(S_n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Find number of elements w in W(S_n) for which [ˆ0,w] is distributive lattice; aim for simple formula without sums/products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterize distributive-interval permutations and count them.

rubrics_metrics.name: 185(j) — total number of distributive intervals in W(S_n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Find total number of intervals in W(S_n) that are distributive lattices; values listed for n≤8 are given (sequence 1,2,16,...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute and possibly conjecture general enumeration or recurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: 185(k) — number of maximal chains M_n formula
rubrics_metrics.description: Show number M_n of maximal chains of W(S_n) is given by product formula M_n = 1^1 3^? ... (exercise states product involving factors (2n−1)!! etc).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove formula for count of maximal chains in weak order.

rubrics_metrics.name: 185(l) — weight product over maximal chains equals r!
rubrics_metrics.description: For cover v⋖w with w=(i,i+1)v define σ(v,w)=i. For maximal chain C define σ(C)=∏ σ(vi−1,vi). Show ∑_{C} σ(C)=r! with sum over all maximal chains of interval [ˆ0,ˆ1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallel identity to 183(g) for weak order weights.

rubrics_metrics.name: 185(m) — relation/similarity between weak and strong Bruhat weight identities
rubrics_metrics.description: Question: Is the similarity between (l) and Exercise 3.183(g) a coincidence? Investigate underlying reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explore structural/combinatorial reasons for analogous weighted-sum identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: 186(a) — product identity for separable permutations' interval FGFs
rubrics_metrics.description: If w∈S_n is separable (Ex.3.14(b)), show F(Λ_w,q) F(V_w,q) = [n]!, where Λ_w=[ˆ0,w] and V_w=[w,ˆ1] in W(S_n) with rank shift convention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factorization result for rank-generating functions of lower and upper intervals for separable permutations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 186(b) — symmetry and unimodality for F(Λ_w,q) and F(V_w,q)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show polynomials F(Λ_w,q) and F(V_w,q) are symmetric and unimodal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove central symmetry and unimodality for these polynomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: 186(c) — formula for F(Λ_w,q) for 231-avoiding permutations
rubrics_metrics.description: Let w be 231-avoiding with a_{n+1}=n+1. Show F(Λ_w,q)=∏_{i=1}^n [c_i]_q where c_i is least positive integer with a_{i+c_i}>a_i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide product expression based on local descent/greater-than structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: 186(d) — question on other permutations with symmetric/dividing property
rubrics_metrics.description: What can be said about other permutations w for which F(Λ_w,q) is symmetric, or divides [n]! ?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-ended classification/characterization problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: 187(a) — M(n) partial order and rank-generating function
rubrics_metrics.description: Define partial order M(n) on 2^[n] via componentwise comparison of subset sizes in a sequence S={a1,...,as}. Show M(n) ≅ J(J(2^n)) and F(M(n),q)=(1+q)(1+q^2)...(1+q^n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish isomorphism to double-join construction and compute rank-generating product formula; Figures 3.66 illustrate M(3),M(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: 187(b) — greedy weak order Gn and isomorphism to M(n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define greedy weak order Gn subset of S_n with specific cover rules. Show Gn ≅ M(n) (or M(n)×?). Describe elements of Gn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate greedy weak order construction to M(n) and identify elements; part (c) asks to describe Gn elements explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: 187(c) — describe elements of Gn
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the elements of the set Gn (greedy weak order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give combinatorial description/classification of permutations in Gn.

rubrics_metrics.name: 188 — Eulerian property of subsequence poset P(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let a=(a1,...,an) integer sequence with no two consecutive equal. Let P(a) be poset of subsequences avoiding consecutive equal elements and ordered by subsequence relation. Show P is Eulerian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove Eulerian property for this subsequence poset.

rubrics_metrics.name: 189 — parity count of coatoms in simplicial Eulerian poset
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P be Eulerian poset rank d+1 with d atoms and P ackslash{ˆ1} a simplicial poset. Show if d is even then number of coatoms is even.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parity constraint in this specialized simplicial/Eulerian setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: 190(a) — cd-index equals sum of all cd monomials
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P_n be poset illustrated (Fig.3.67) with restriction patterns. Show P_n is Eulerian with cd-index equal to sum of all cd-monomials of degree n (deg c=1, deg d=2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute cd-index and show it equals sum over all monomials of appropriate degree.

rubrics_metrics.name: 190(b) — generating function for maximal chains M(n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let M(n) be number of maximal chains of P_n. Show ∑_{n≥0} M(n) x^n = 1 / (2x) * (1 − sqrt(1−2x−2x^2)) (? exercise indicates rational expression).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish EGF/OGF for maximal chain counts; explicit closed form given in exercise.

rubrics_metrics.name: 191(a) — join of Eulerian posets is Eulerian
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P and Q Eulerian posets. Show P * Q (join as defined in eq.3.86) is Eulerian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove closure of Eulerian property under join operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 191(b) — multiplicativity of cd-index under join
rubrics_metrics.description: Show Φ_{P*Q}(c,d) = Φ_P(c,d) Φ_Q(c,d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: cd-index is multiplicative over join; prove product formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: 192 — nonnegativity of cd-index for Gorenstein* posets
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P be Cohen-Macaulay and Eulerian (Gorenstein*). Show cd-index Φ_P(c,d) has nonnegative coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove positivity for cd-index in Gorenstein* (topologically restricted) cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: 193(a) — example of Eulerian poset with negative cd-index coefficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Give an example of an Eulerian poset whose cd-index has a negative coefficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct counterexample showing nonnegativity fails without Cohen-Macaulay/Gorenstein* hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: 193(b) — Eulerian poset with negative flag h-vector entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Give example of Eulerian poset P whose flag h-vector β_P has a negative entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengthen (a) by finding negative flag h-vector value.

rubrics_metrics.name: 194 — dimension of space spanned by flag f-vectors of rank-symmetric Eulerian posets
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P finite graded poset rank n with pi elements of rank i. P rank-symmetric if pi=pn−i for 0≤i≤n. Find dimension d(n) of space spanned over Q by flag f- or h-vectors of all Eulerian posets of rank n with every interval rank-symmetric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linear-algebraic/combinatorial dimension-counting problem for flag-vector span under symmetry constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: 195 — dimension dn(k) for k-Eulerian posets
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix k≥1 and let Fn(k) be space spanned by flag f-vectors of graded posets rank n with ˆ0 and ˆ1 such that every interval of rank k is Eulerian (k-Eulerian). For odd k=2j+1 show dn(2j+1) generating function identity: ∑_{n≥0} dn(2j+1) x^n = 1 + ∑_{n≥1} x(1+x)(1+x^{2j})/(1−x^{2j+2}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute dimensions of spaces of flag-vectors under local Eulerian constraints; generating function provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: 196(a) — factorial function inequality in binomial poset
rubrics_metrics.description: Show if B(n) is factorial function of binomial poset then B(n) B(n+1) ≥ B(n+1) B(n)?? (exercise states B(n)^2 ≤ B(n)B(n+1)??). Specifically show B(n)^2 ≤ B(n) B(n+1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inequality relations for factorial function B(n) in binomial posets.

rubrics_metrics.name: 196(b) — classify factorial functions of binomial posets
rubrics_metrics.description: What functions B(n) are factorial functions of binomial posets? In particular can one have B(n)=F_1 F_2 ... F_n where F_i are Fibonacci numbers?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterize allowable factorial sequences for binomial posets; specific Fibonacci-product question included.

rubrics_metrics.name: 197 — uncountably many nonisomorphic binomial posets with same B(n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show existence of uncountably many pairwise nonisomorphic binomial posets P_α such that (a) they all have same factorial function B(n), and (b) each P_α has a maximal chain ˆ0=t0⋖t1⋖... such that P_α = ⋃_{n≥0} [ˆ0, t_n].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct continuum many nonisomorphic examples sharing same factorial function and chain union property.

rubrics_metrics.name: 198 — classification of Eulerian binomial posets
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P be Eulerian binomial poset (every interval Eulerian). Show either every n-interval is boolean algebra B_n or every n-interval is butterfly poset (ladder) A2⊕... (exercise states two possible local types).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify local interval-types possible for Eulerian binomial posets.

rubrics_metrics.name: 199 — finite distributive lattices that are binomial posets
rubrics_metrics.description: Find all finite distributive lattices L that are binomial posets, except axiom of containing an infinite chain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterize distributive lattices with binomial poset factorial counting properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: 200 — zeta polynomial of q=2 binomial poset n-interval
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P_n be n-interval of q=2 binomial poset of Example 3.18.3(e), with B(n)=2^{n choose 2} n!. Show Z(P_n,m)= ∑_{G} χ_G(m) where sum over all simple graphs G on vertex set [n] and χ_G chromatic polynomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express zeta polynomial as sum of chromatic polynomials over graphs (equation (3.132)).

rubrics_metrics.name: 201(a) — triangular poset algebra is upper-triangular matrices
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P be locally finite poset with ˆ0, every maximal chain infinite and every interval graded; triangular poset if function B(m,n) counts maximal chains per interval. Define T(P) subalgebra of incidence algebra of functions constant on equal-rank endpoints. Show T(P) ≅ algebra of infinite upper-triangular matrices [a_{ij}] with entries f(i,j)/B(i,j) mapping given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct isomorphism from incidence-algebra subalgebra to matrix algebra via normalized function entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: 201(b) — semimodularity condition in triangular lattices
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L triangular lattice, set D(n)=B(n,n+1). Show L is (upper) semimodular iff for all n≥m+2, B(m,n)/B(m+1,n) = 1 + ∑_{i=0}^{n−m−2} D(m)/[D(m+i)D(m+i+1)] (exercise provides identity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterize semimodularity via chain-count function ratios and D(n).

rubrics_metrics.name: 201(c) — atomicity criterion for triangular lattice
rubrics_metrics.description: If D(n)≠0 for all n≥0 then show L is atomic. Use (b) to show converse is true if L semimodular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate nonvanishing of D(n) to atomic property in triangular lattices and converses under semimodularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: 202 — shuffle poset interval canonical factorization multiplicative functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Let shuffle poset W_{∞,∞} defined in Ex.7.48(g). Define multiplicative functions f in incidence algebra constant on canonical isomorphism types Wij and multiplicative across canonical factors. Let generating functions F(x,y)=∑ f_{ij} x^i y^j. Show convolution corresponds to certain substitutions: F(x,y)=F(x,G_0 y) etc and derive formula involving F0,G0 and convolutions: G^{-1} * F etc (exercise gives explicit functional identities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate multiplicativity and convolution in incidence algebra into functional equations for formal power series F,G; show substitution identities and relation involving inverses (convolution).

rubrics_metrics.name: 203 — determinant formula for permutation-with-remainder generating functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix integer sequence 0<=a1<...<ar<m with residues mod m etc. Define fk(n) counts of permutations of certain residues with descent conditions and generating functions F_k(x). Define Φ_j(x) as specific series. Show linear system F Ψ = identity vector and solve to express F_k(x) as quotient of two determinants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set up and solve linear equations among generating functions resulting in determinant expressions for F_k.

rubrics_metrics.name: 204(a) — incidence-algebra inversion identity for graded intervals with subset-Möbius
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P locally finite with graded intervals. For S⊆[n] define [s,t]_S and µ_S(s,t) its Möbius function. Define g(s,t)=1 if s=t else (1+z)^n if ℓ(s,t)=n ??? and h(s,t)=... Show h = g^{-1} in I(P). (Exercise defines g,h and asks to show relation.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish formal inversion in incidence algebra with z-parameter and subset-Möbius weightings; use combinatorial Möbius sums.

rubrics_metrics.name: 204(b) — h(n) and generating series identity for binomial poset
rubrics_metrics.description: For binomial poset P let h(n)=h(s,t) when ℓ(s,t)=n. Show ∑_{n≥0} x^n / B(n) (1 + h(n)/(1+x)^n) = 1 + ∑_{n≥1} ... (exercise states algebraic identity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive series identity linking h(n), factorial B(n) and generating functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 204(c) — Gn(q,z) generating function for permutations by des and inv
rubrics_metrics.description: Define G_n(q,z)=∑_{w∈S_n} z^{des(w)} q^{inv(w)}. Show identity: (1+z) ∑_{n≥0} G_n(q,z) x^n / (n)! = ... (exercise provides specific product/exponential generating relation). Setting q=1 recovers Proposition 1.4.5 and Eulerian polynomial identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove bivariate generating-function identity linking statistics des and inv across symmetric groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: 205(a) — example 1-differential poset not Young's lattice
rubrics_metrics.description: Give example of 1-differential poset that is not isomorphic to Young's lattice Y nor to Ω_1^∞ Y[n] for any n (Ω_1^∞ denotes some truncation/operation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct nonstandard 1-differential poset.

rubrics_metrics.name: 205(b) — enumeration counts of nonisomorphic 1-differential posets up to rank
rubrics_metrics.description: Show counts of nonisomorphic 1-differential posets up to rank: 2 up to rank 6, 35 up to rank 7, 643 up to rank 8, 44605 up to rank 9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerative verification/computation of classification counts to given ranks.

rubrics_metrics.name: 205(c) — example of 1-differential poset not isomorphic to Y or Ω_1^∞ P
rubrics_metrics.description: Give example of 1-differential poset that is not isomorphic to Y nor to Ω_1^∞ P where P is 1-differential up to some rank n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct another nonstandard example; variation on (a).

rubrics_metrics.name: 206 — classification of 1-differential lattices
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that the only 1-differential lattices are Young's lattice Y and Z1 (some specified lattice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove classification result narrowing possibilities to two lattices.

rubrics_metrics.name: 207 — Hasse walk generating series in r-differential poset
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P be r-differential poset and define A_k(q) as in eq.(3.110). Write α(n→n+1→n→n+1→n) for number of Hasse walks of pattern U D U D. Show ∑_{n≥0} α(n→) q^n = F(P,q) (2r q^2 A_2(q) + r q^3 A_3(q) + q^4 A_4(q)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate counts of specific short Hasse walks to generating-function expressions involving A_k(q) and rank-generating function F(P,q).

rubrics_metrics.name: 208(a) — valid t-words weight formula in r-differential poset
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P r-differential and t∈P. Define valid t-word w in letters U and D meaning wˆ0,t ≠ 0 etc. For each position define ai and bi counts. Show ⟨w ˆ0,t⟩ = e(t) r^{#S} ∏_i binomial(ai,bi−ai) (exercise gives expression) where e(t) defined in Ex.3.21.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute weight/inner-product for monomials in raising/lowering operators in differential poset context.

rubrics_metrics.name: 208(b) — specialization deduced from (a) for ρ(t)=n
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce from (a) that when ρ(t)=n then ⟨w ˆ0,t⟩ = α(0→n) r^{#S} ∏_i ... (exercise gives simplified form).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simplify general formula for specific rank values; use notation α(0→n).

rubrics_metrics.name: 208(c) — special-case UDUU evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce special case UD UU ˆ0,P ⟨·⟩ = 2 r^2 (r+1) and recover result of Ex.3.207.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute explicit numerical evaluation for specific word sequence of U/D.

rubrics_metrics.name: 209 — normal-order formula for UD/DU operators
rubrics_metrics.description: If D U − U D = 1 and UD=1?? Show (UD)^n = ∑_{k=0}^n S(n,k) U^k D^k where S(n,k) are Stirling numbers of second kind (equation (3.134)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operator-algebra identity expressing power of UD in normal-ordered monomials with Stirling coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: 210 — balanced words commute under DU−UD=1
rubrics_metrics.description: A word in U,D balanced if #U=#D. Show that if D U − U D = 1 then any two balanced words in U and D commute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algebraic combinatorics identity about commutation of balanced monomials under Heisenberg-type commutation relation.
